title: Singapore 3D
about:
Singapore's centre and the Greater Southern Waterfront: Marina Bay all round, the CBD and Raffles Place, the Civic District, the Singapore River, Chinatown, Bugis, Kampong Glam and Little India, Kallang Basin and the Sports Hub, Orchard Road, River Valley, Tiong Bahru, the City Terminals, HarbourFront, Keppel Bay, Mount Faber and Sentosa: 54 subzones of URA's Master Plan 2019, 32.6 km². Around them, on the land side, a 500 m band of plain block masses; beyond it the island's towers of 30 m and more and Johor Bahru's across the strait as masses too, on painted ground, and the hills and shores to about 30 km.

Real, from open data, each thing where it is: the building footprints (OpenStreetMap's outlines and building parts, about 9,500 pieces; HDB's own block outlines where OSM has none); the public housing blocks' storeys from HDB's Property Information; the towers' heights from published sources (the CTBUH's Skyscraper Center and Wikipedia, 47 towers and landmarks); OSM's mapped heights and storeys for most other buildings; the ground from Copernicus GLO-30, made bare earth (towers and canopy taken out, the named hills lifted back to their surveyed heights); roads, bridges, railways, the bay, the river, reservoirs, beaches, parks and land use from OpenStreetMap, with its bus lanes, signals and crossings; the far land's colours from ESA WorldCover 2021; the sun on 23 March, clock time SGT (UTC+8).

Estimated, not measured: a quarter of the buildings have no height in OSM and stand at the median of their tagged neighbours of a similar size (one in ten at a default 10.5 m); HDB blocks at 2.8 m a storey plus 4 m, shophouses at 4.5 m plus 4 m an upper storey, other storeys at 3.5 m; the far masses at OSM's heights where mapped, else guessed from their kind.

Modelled after photos, not measured: the landmarks' shapes (the Marina Bay Sands SkyPark and the towers' lean, the Supertrees and the OCBC Skyway, the Flower Dome and Cloud Forest, the ArtScience Museum, the Esplanade's shells, the Singapore Flyer, the Helix Bridge, the Merlion, the National Stadium's dome, the Victoria clock tower, the Old Supreme Court's dome, the Sultan Mosque's domes, Sri Mariamman's gopuram, the Buddha Tooth Relic Temple's roofs) and their colours; some of their heights are estimates (the Cloud Forest, the gopuram, the domes). Landmarks without a figure take the generic styles.

Invented to look plausible: the facades (Singapore's styles drawn by the shader: HDB slabs with accent paint, corridors and void decks, shophouses with louvred shutters and five-foot ways, condos, Sentosa's villas, colonial render and colonnades, the CBD's glass, fins and granite; window grids and colours from palettes, not photographed; which side of an HDB block has its corridors is a guess); the rooftop clutter (lift motor rooms, water tanks, solar panels, condensers); the trees (placed by rule along OSM's roads and in its parks, their species after NParks' roadside planting: rain trees, angsana, tembusu, palms); the road markings' layout (after LTA's British-style code), the pavements and paving; the cars, buses and taxis, the traffic and where they park; which windows are lit at night, the lamps, the floodlights and the landmark glows.

Credits: contains information from Master Plan 2019 Subzone Boundary (No Sea), HDB Existing Building, HDB Property Information and Master Plan 2019 Building layer accessed on 6 October 2026 from data.gov.sg which is made available under the terms of the Singapore Open Data Licence version 1.0; © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL), via the Overpass API and a BBBike extract; contains modified Copernicus DEM GLO-30 data © DLR e.V. 2010-2014 and © Airbus Defence and Space GmbH 2014-2018 provided under COPERNICUS by the European Union and ESA; © ESA WorldCover project 2021, contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data (2021) processed by the ESA WorldCover consortium (CC BY 4.0). Tower heights are facts from the CTBUH's Skyscraper Center and Wikipedia; reference photos from Wikimedia Commons were only looked at, not redistributed. The derived data (buildings, roads, trees and the rest) is a derivative database of OpenStreetMap and is offered under the Open Database License 1.0 (ODbL): it is the data files this page loads, served next to it (tiles, blocks, markings, trees, shores, cars and rooftops beside this page) and made by this repository's pipeline; the rendered images are Produced Works, attributed as above. Rendered with three.js and its meshoptimizer decoder (both MIT licence).
